{
  "summary": "Richardson, Hu, Moss, and Sabharwal propose semantic fragments to probe NLI models' reasoning on logic, monotonicity, and quantification. State-of-the-art models like BERT perform poorly on these fragments despite centrality to NLI. With brief finetuning and inoculation, a BERT-based model masters all logic and monotonicity fragments while retaining established benchmark performance.",
  "limitations": "",
  "approach": "semantic fragments",
  "evaluation": "NLI benchmark",
  "abstract": "Richardson, Hu, Moss, and Sabharwal propose semantic fragments—systematically generated NLI datasets each targeting a distinct semantic phenomenon—for probing, and efficiently improving, such capabilities of linguistic models.",
  "introduction": "Richardson, Hu, Moss, and Sabharwal propose semantic fragments to investigate the extent to which state-of-the-art NLI models capture central semantic phenomena.",
  "conclusion": "With only a few minutes of additional finetuning, a BERT-based model can master all of these logic and monotonicity fragments while retaining its performance on established NLI benchmarks."
